title: EventEnvelope
description:
Events are a durable stream with consumer groups, at-least-once delivery and ordering within a session partition - not fire-and-forget pub/sub, which silently drops recording.completed when a consumer is down. The envelope is the second of exactly two contact points between the Go and Python halves.

Payloads are typed per event type through the allOf below. Only the events the platform currently emits are typed; the rest keep an open payload deliberately, because inventing a shape for an event no code produces yet is how a data model gets locked wrong. THE RULE: an event type must have a payload schema in this file before any code emits it. An open payload does not generate a type - it generates map[string]any, dict and Record<string, unknown> - so an event left open is an event with no SDK contract.

eventId.description: Doubles as the idempotency key for webhook delivery. 128 bits, because consumers store these and the width cannot be changed after issue.

version.description: Per-event version. Additive by default; behaviour never changes silently.

sequence.description: Monotonic within the session partition. Ordering is guaranteed here and nowhere else.

occurredAt.description: RFC 3339 with a UTC offset and millisecond precision. The pattern is asserted alongside the format because format assertion is opt-in in most validators, so a format keyword alone would be documentation rather than a check.

traceId.description: W3C trace id. One trace per turn, not per session.

EventType.description: agent.state_changed is the most important event for user experience: a user who can see 'thinking' waits, while a user staring at silence talks over the agent.

UsageUnit.description: What a provider bills by. Singular, because a price is stated per one of it.

LayerMs.description: One layer of a turn's latency in milliseconds, as the agent framework measured it. Absent when the framework did not measure that layer for the turn, never zero in its place.

configHash.description: Ties this session to the exact resolved config it ran under, which is what makes it explainable afterwards.

SessionSignalPayload.description: The consumer-defined passthrough. Its data is open by design: this is the extension point that stops a consumer forking when they need to carry something the platform has no opinion about.

relayed.description: Whether media is going through a TURN relay rather than a direct path. Expect 10-20% of connections to relay, higher on mobile. Reported per connection because relay bandwidth is metered per tenant and doubles as a diagnostic: a rising relay share means the consumer's network changed, not that the platform did.

downtimeMs.description: Mobile clients drop constantly, so reconnection is the SDK's job rather than the consumer's. This is how long the gap actually was.

pool.description: Which worker pool took the job. Recorded per session so a second pool can be introduced and observed without guessing which sessions it served.

WakeSource.description: How a dormant agent was woken: name, somebody said its name; manual, somebody pressed a wake control, which the agent treats as that person calling it.

AgentStateChangedPayload.description: The single most important event for user experience. A consumer renders this directly, so it is typed rather than left for them to discover at runtime. An agent that waits to be called by name also says whether it is dormant, and when awake who woke it, as an opaque participant id and never a name or what they said, so the event stays safe to log. Sent again, with the same state and no previousState, when only that changes.

dormant.description: Present only when the session's addressing mode waits to be called. True: the agent hears the call but answers nobody until its name is said.

AgentTurnMetricsPayload.description: Where one agent turn's latency went, layer by layer, measured inside the worker. The user-side layers come from the user's message that the reply answers, so a turn the agent opened itself (a greeting) carries none of them. A consumer compares e2eLatencyMs with what it measured itself; the difference is the network and playout on its side.

turn.description: The agent's turn within the session, counted from 0.

endOfTurnDelayMs.description: From the end of the user's speech to the decision that their turn ended.

transcriptionDelayMs.description: From the end of the user's speech to the final transcript.

llmNodeTtfsMs.description: LLM time to the first sentence handed to TTS.

ttsNodeTtfbMs.description: TTS time to first audio byte.

playbackLatencyMs.description: From the first audio frame forwarded to playback reported started.

e2eLatencyMs.description: From the end of the user's speech to the agent starting to speak.

filler.description: True when the reply was slow enough that a filler phrase played ahead of it (agent.speech.fillers): ttsNodeTtfbMs and e2eLatencyMs then count from the filler, the first audio the caller heard, while the LLM layers still show what was slow. Present only when a filler played.

serial.description: True when the turn went serial: its first sentence reached TTS more than 500 ms after the LLM's first token (llmNodeTtfsMs minus llmNodeTtftMs), so the reply waited on more than its first sentence and its latency tracked the length of the reply. Present only when both LLM layers were measured.

language.description: The language the agent replied in, as a session language tag. Present only in a session that switches languages (agent.languageSwitching), where it can differ from the session's language, so its turns can be measured per language.

UsageItem.description: One provider, model and unit's consumption so far. An item the price table has no row for is unpriced and carries no cost, because a zero would read as free.

SessionUsagePayload.description: What the session has consumed and what it cost in INR. Sent after each agent turn as a running figure and once more when the session ends; the last one sent is the one to keep.

final.description: True for the figure taken when the session ended.

costInr.description: The sum of the priced items. A floor, not a total, while unpricedItems is above zero.
